task_instance: Created a sample schedule.csv with 5 conference sessions (title, date, start, end, room, speaker), then wrote a Python script using the 'ics' package to build one VEVENT per session with time zone Europe/Berlin, room mapped to LOCATION and speaker mapped to DESCRIPTION, and wrote the result to conference.ics. Then validated by re-parsing conference.ics with the ics package and confirming the event count matches the CSV row count.
evidence: Installed the 'ics' package via `pip install ics` (succeeded, version 0.7.3). Wrote schedule.csv with 5 rows. Wrote build_ics.py which reads schedule.csv, builds an ics.Calendar with one Event per row (Event.begin/end localized to Europe/Berlin via zoneinfo, Event.location=room, Event.description=speaker), and serializes to conference.ics. Ran `python3 build_ics.py` -> 'Wrote conference.ics with 5 events (from 5 CSV rows)'. Inspected conference.ics: contains 5 BEGIN:VEVENT...END:VEVENT blocks with correct SUMMARY/LOCATION/DESCRIPTION and DTSTART/DTEND correctly converted from Europe/Berlin local time to UTC (e.g. 2026-10-05 09:00 Berlin -> DTSTART:20261005T070000Z, consistent with CEST UTC+2 before DST ends in late Oct). Validation step: re-parsed conference.ics with ics.Calendar(...) and compared len(cal.events) (5) to the CSV row count (5) -- match confirmed, printed 'VALIDATION OK: counts match' along with all 5 parsed events showing correct name/time/location/description. Files produced: schedule.csv, build_ics.py, conference.ics, all under the work directory.
